title: 1 · Sounds, spelling and the alphabet
blurb: Read any German word aloud: the letters that differ from English, the umlauts, the two ‹ch› sounds and where the stress goes.

title: 2 · Greetings: ‹Sie› and ‹du›
blurb: Greet people at any time of day, give your name and where you are from, and choose between ‹Sie› and ‹du›.

title: 3 · ‹der›, ‹die›, ‹das› and plurals
blurb: Learn every noun with its ‹der›, ‹die› or ‹das›, spot the endings that give the gender away, and make plurals with ‹die›.

title: 4 · ‹sein› and ‹haben›: I am, I have
blurb: Say who you are, what you do, how old you are and what you have, with the two most important German verbs.

title: 5 · Present tense: regular verbs
blurb: Say what people do, every day or right now, with the right ending for every person.

title: 6 · Verb second: ‹Heute arbeite ich›
blurb: Start a sentence with a time or a place and keep the verb in second place, the way German does.

title: 7 · W-questions and yes/no questions
blurb: Ask who, what, where, when and how, and ask yes/no questions, without any do.

title: 8 · Numbers, time and prices
blurb: Count to a thousand, tell the time, and understand prices in euros.

title: 9 · Stem-changing verbs: ‹fahren›, ‹essen›, ‹nehmen›
blurb: Use the verbs that change their vowel, and order food with ‹Ich nehme› and ‹Was nimmst du?›

title: 10 · Accusative: ‹den›, ‹einen›
blurb: Say what you buy, need and have, with ‹den› and ‹einen› for masculine nouns, and read who does what from the article.

title: 11 · ‹nicht› and ‹kein›
blurb: Say what you don't have and don't do, choosing ‹kein› before a noun and putting ‹nicht› in the right place.

title: 12 · ‹mein›, ‹dein›, ‹sein›, ‹ihr›
blurb: Talk about your family and other people's with my, your, his, her, our and their, with the right ending.

title: 13 · Likes: ‹gern›, ‹mögen›, ‹lieber›
blurb: Say what you like doing, what you prefer, and which things and people you like.

title: 14 · Modal verbs: ‹können›, ‹müssen›, ‹wollen›, ‹möchten›
blurb: Say what you can, have to, want to and would like to do, with the second verb at the end.

title: 15 · Separable verbs: ‹aufstehen›, ‹anrufen›
blurb: Describe your daily routine with verbs like ‹aufstehen› and ‹einkaufen›, sending the prefix to the end.

title: 16 · The sentence bracket
blurb: Build travel sentences with two verb parts: the conjugated verb second and the other part at the very end.

title: 17 · Dative: ‹dem›, ‹der›, ‹mit›, ‹bei›
blurb: Get around town with ‹mit›, ‹zu›, ‹bei›, ‹von› and ‹nach›, using the dative articles ‹dem›, ‹der› and ‹den›.

title: 18 · Pronouns: ‹ich›, ‹mich›, ‹mir›
blurb: Say me, you, him and her in the right case, and talk about how you feel with ‹mir› and ‹dir›.

title: 19 · Prepositions of place and time
blurb: Say where something is and where you are going, and use ‹am›, ‹im› and ‹um› for times.

title: 20 · Imperative: ‹du›, ‹ihr›, ‹Sie›
blurb: Tell someone what to do, politely to a stranger and simply to a friend.

title: 21 · Perfekt: what happened
blurb: Say what you did yesterday or last weekend with ‹haben› or ‹sein› and a past participle.

title: 22 · ‹war› and ‹hatte›
blurb: Say where you were and what you had with ‹war› and ‹hatte›, and recognize ‹konnte› and ‹musste›.

title: 23 · Adjectives and comparing
blurb: Describe clothes and things, and say what is cheaper, bigger or best.

title: 24 · ‹und›, ‹oder›, ‹aber›, ‹denn›, ‹wenn›
blurb: Join two sentences with and, or, but, because and if, with the verb in the right place.

title: 25 · False friends: ‹Gift›, ‹Chef›, ‹will›
blurb: Avoid the German words that look English but mean something else, and say I'm hot, hungry or right the German way.
